transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-03-19
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes (planned 60)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Riley Chen (Redwood SE), Martin Holt (BlueCrest CTO), Aisha Khan (BlueCrest Head of Data Eng), Leo Park (BlueCrest Security Architect)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align on pilot acceptance criteria (security/compliance), workload sizing for benchmarks, timeline for a 3-4 week pilot, and immediate action items to exchange docs and run a baseline throughput/latency test. Customer emphasized SOC 2 + ISO posture, SSO (SAML), RBAC, long-lived audit logs, and data residency for EU shipments.

Topics Covered:
- Pilot success criteria (latency, throughput, quality/regression thresholds)
- Workload profile (median token lengths, avg requests/day, peak patterns)
- Benchmarks to run and metrics to collect (95th lat, p50, QPS, cost per 1k tokens)
- Security/compliance: SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration, data retention
- Deployment mode tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC)
- Timeline and milestones for kickoff and evaluation

Transcript:
00:00:03 Jamie (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We planned about an hour today, just to lock down acceptance criteria and figure out the benchmark sizing that Riley will run. Martin, want to kick off with top priorities?
00:00:17 Martin (BlueCrest): Yeah, thanks. Main thing for us is security, right, and predictable performance. We ship EU and NA, and for the pilot we need to prove low latency and also show we can meet SOC 2 copy, I mean SOC 2 expectations, and ISO is important to our procurement.
00:00:34 Jamie: Totally. When you say SOC 2 expectations, do you mean you need Redwood's attestation docs and evidence about controls, or do you need us to run in your private VPC for the pilot?
00:00:46 Martin: Both, slightly different audiences. Procurement wants the SOC 2 Type II, and legal wants ISO summary. Security (Leo) will validate integration points: SSO via SAML, RBAC mapping to AD, KMS for key control, and audit log retention of at least 12 months.
00:01:02 Leo (BlueCrest): Yeah and just to add, audit logs need to include: request metadata, model version, user id or API key mapping, region, and any redaction events. Also retention policies, immutability/append-only, and an export path for our SIEM — ideally Kafka or S3.
00:01:20 Riley (Redwood SE): Got it. We have audit log exports and integrations (S3/Kinesis) in Dedicated and Private modes; hosted can stream logs to customer S3 with proper config as well. There might be slight differences in retention default but we can configure retention for the pilot.
00:01:33 Aisha (BlueCrest): Ok great. On the perf side — we expect a production-like mix: about 1200 avg tokens per convo with many short requests too. Peak pattern on Mondays, potentially up to ~150-200 rps during 15-minute bursts. Can you size hardware for that?
00:01:52 Riley: That's helpful. For spikes of 150-200 rps we need to know the model family and requested max new tokens; but baseline, with a quantized LLM variant and batching, Dedicated pools can handle that with correct autoscale. For benchmarking we'll need sample prompts and a token distribution so we can mimic the mix.
00:02:10 Martin: We'll provide a 2k request corpus that represents the mixture — some long, some short. Success criteria: 95th perc latency under 200ms for short requests (<50 tokens) and under 800ms for long ones (500-1500 tokens). Also cost target: keep token cost below $0.0015 per input token averaged across workload.
00:02:30 Jamie: Clarify — is the 95th target a hard stop for acceptance or a stretch goal?
00:02:36 Martin: Hard stop for the pilot to be considered successful by product. Security gating is equally non-negotiable.
00:02:44 Leo: Also need to know about data residency — EU-only for EU customers. Pilot can run in our EU region, but we need to see network topology and that logs do not egress to US without consent.
00:02:56 Riley: We can pin region routing and show topology diagrams. For pilot scale we can use EU-dedicated nodes or a private deployment in their VPC if needed.
00:03:10 Jamie: Ok, let's step through the security checklist so we capture next steps.
00:03:16 Jamie: SOC 2 and ISO: we'll share the attestation docs and our SOC 2 Type II report.
00:03:20 Martin: Good.
00:03:22 Jamie: SSO/SAML — we support SAML 2.0 with group/role mapping; we can map to AD groups for RBAC. Any special requirements?
00:03:30 Leo: We need SCIM for automated provisioning if possible, or at least an SSO flow that avoids manual invites. And SAML attributes must be able to carry role claims. Also MFA enforcement via IdP.
00:03:43 Riley: SCIM is available on Dedicated and Private; hosted supports SAML and manual provisioning workflows. For the pilot we can enable SCIM if you prefer Dedicated.
00:03:54 Aisha: For the pilot, we'd rather not do a full Dedicated contract up front. Can we do a hosted pilot with SAML + SCIM enabled?
00:04:02 Jamie: For short pilots we often do hosted with an elevated security posture and SAML; SCIM can be enabled but sometimes is gated. We'll check and confirm.
00:04:10 Martin: If SCIM is not possible in hosted, it's a blocker for us for user management. Procurement will push back unless we can show automated provisioning.
00:04:20 Riley: Understood. We'll flag that as high priority in the follow-ups.

00:04:34 Aisha: About RBAC, we need role separation: devs, operators, analytics read-only, and security auditing roles. Can you map to custom roles?
00:04:43 Riley: Yes, we have custom role creation and can map those roles from SAML/group claims. We also emit audit events for role changes.
00:04:50 Leo: One more: encryption keys — we must be able to use our KMS or at least BYOK for certain artifacts. Is BYOK available?
00:04:58 Jamie: BYOK is available on Private, and there's a managed KMS integration for Dedicated. Hosted supports customer-managed keys in some configurations — we'll include the exact options in the doc pack.
00:05:10 Martin: Good. Ok benchmarks — tell us what you'll run and how the results will be presented.
00:05:18 Riley: Plan: 1) Baseline single-client latency profile (p50/p95) for sample prompts across the token length mix. 2) Load runs: ramp to target QPS (50, 100, 200) for 15-30 minute windows to see autoscale behavior and p95 tail. 3) Cost estimation run to show tokens consumed and per-token cost. We'll provide a workbook with raw traces, percentiles, and recommendations (batching/caching/quantization).
00:05:41 Aisha: Will you anonymize logs? We will send sample data that might include order IDs and PII — do you need us to mask?
00:05:48 Riley: For the test harness, we prefer synthetic or redacted data. If you supply PII, we'll handle it under our data processing agreement, but for speed, redacted samples are ideal.
00:05:58 Martin: We'll scrub sensitive fields and provide a mapping doc.
00:06:03 Jamie: Timeline idea: today we exchange docs (SOC2, ISO, redaction rules) this week. Riley runs an initial baseline next week (week of 24th). Then a focused 3-week pilot: week 1 baseline and tuning, week 2 load tests and regression checks, week 3 final validation and acceptance. Does that align?
00:06:20 Martin: Sounds reasonable. Procurement will want a 4-week window, but we can condense if results look good.
00:06:26 Leo: We also need a short security questionnaire filled out — standard vendor security questionnaire. Can you do that?
00:06:32 Jamie: Yes, we can fill out the vendor questionnaire. We'll attach it with the SOC docs.

00:06:50 Riley: Quick technical note: when we report p95 for long-run requests, we include decoding time and network. If you want box-only numbers we can separate runtime-only latencies (no network) — useful to compare hardware choices.
00:07:04 Aisha: Yes, separate runtime and end-to-end is helpful. Include tokenization overheads too.
00:07:10 Riley: Will do. Also, caching: if you have a lot of repeated prefixes, prefix cache can drop latencies dramatically. If that's part of your access pattern, let us know.
00:07:20 Martin: We do have templated instructions for some workflows, so caching could help. We'll describe frequency of repeats in the dataset.

00:07:45 Jamie: Let's capture acceptance criteria explicitly for the pilot so everyone's aligned. I'll read them and please interrupt with edits.
00:07:52 Jamie: Pilot acceptance criteria (draft): 1) Security: Redwood provides SOC 2 Type II attestation and ISO27001 summary; SAML-based SSO with role mapping or SCIM; RBAC roles mapped to AD; audit logs exported to customer S3/Kafka with 12+ months retention; KMS or BYOK options documented. 2) Performance/Capacity: p95 latency under 200ms for short (<50 tokens), p95 under 800ms for long (500-1500 tokens) during baseline and under ≤ 2x during peak spikes; autoscale should handle 150-200 rps bursts. 3) Cost: average token cost below $0.0015 per input token or a documented mitigation plan. 4) Quality: No regression on defined test sets; scoring above baseline acceptance thresholds (we'll define metrics). 5) Timeline: Pilot results and security docs submitted within 4 weeks.
00:08:44 Martin: Couple tweaks: make SSO/SCIM non-negotiable for production acceptance. For pilot, SAML w/manual provisioning is acceptable but must have SCIM on the roadmap with dates. Also call out data residency (EU) as mandatory for EU traffic.
00:08:58 Jamie: Noted — will update.

00:09:12 Riley: On the audit log spec: we'll include fields you requested and show a sample event schema. Also add model version and prompt hash to help with debugging.
00:09:21 Leo: Prompt hash is good for linking to original without exposing content. But we need evidence of redaction events recorded as separate audit entries when de-identification happens.
00:09:30 Riley: We can emit redaction events. We'll show how they appear and the retention policy.

00:10:00 Aisha: Any concerns about bleeding tokens across tenants? We need strong tenant isolation.
00:10:07 Jamie: Tenant isolation is fundamental; we run per-tenant models or per-tenant prefixes depending on deployment and never mix KV caches across tenants. Riley, can you elaborate?
00:10:15 Riley: Right — per-tenant isolation on Dedicated and Private. Hosted is multi-tenant but with strong namespace separation and logical isolation; for regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private.
00:10:27 Martin: For pilot we can tolerate hosted if isolation and logs are proven. But production likely Dedicated or Private.

00:10:45 Jamie: Ok, let's talk about SRE/ops support during the pilot — escalation paths and SLAs if we hit a perf issue.
00:10:53 Riley: For pilots we offer on-call SE coverage during scheduled load tests. Dedicated contracts include SLO-backed SLAs. We'll detail the escalation flow in the follow-up doc.
00:11:04 Martin: Good. Also, can you provide a sample SOW for a 4-week pilot with deliverables?
00:11:11 Jamie: Yes, we'll send a draft SOW with milestones: kickoff, baseline run, tuning, load tests, final report.

00:11:30 (brief crosstalk)

00:11:50 Martin: Quick note on benchmarks: include measures for cold-start and warm cache behaviors. Some of our workloads are highly bursty.
00:12:00 Riley: We'll include cold vs warm from KV cache + cold model load times.
00:12:06 Aisha: Also include one end-to-end test from our frontend to ensure middleware latency is measured.
00:12:12 Riley: Noted.

00:12:40 Jamie: Any competitor comparisons that matter? Martin mentioned Anthropic before the call — are you evaluating them in parallel?
00:12:48 Martin: We've got a short list: Anthropic and Bedrock for managed endpoints. Main reasons we're talking to Redwood: better observability and playbook for production deployment.
00:12:59 Jamie: Great feedback. We'll include a performance/cost slide versus public numbers where it's helpful.

00:13:20 (15 minute marker)

00:13:22 Riley: For the benchmark runner I'll need: sample prompt corpus, token distribution, expected max tokens per request, and 1-2 representative payloads that include any non-text fields. Also, point us to the SIEM ingestion endpoint for test log exports if you want live streaming.
00:13:41 Martin: We'll assemble those artifacts and aim to send them by Friday.

00:13:55 Leo: On audit: we require immutable logs for compliance. Do you support WORM or append-only storage guarantees?
00:14:04 Riley: We can configure exports to your S3 with object lock enabled to ensure immutability on your side. For our managed logs, retention windows are adjustable, but for compliance we recommend export + your retention.
00:14:16 Leo: Good. Also need a record of access to the logs (who pulled them).
00:14:20 Jamie: Access logs for exports and downloads are included; we'll map that out.

00:14:45 Aisha: Regarding cost, can you simulate a cost projection for our expected 1M tokens/day volume?
00:14:53 Riley: Yes, after we run the load tests we'll produce a per-day and per-month cost projection, including suggestions for quantization/packing to reduce unit cost.
00:15:00 Martin: Let's make sure cost projections include worst-case for retries and higher decode length.

00:15:12 Jamie: We're at about 15 minutes into the call; anything else critical we haven't covered?
00:15:19 Martin: One small thing — procurement will need a standard DPA and data flow diagram for the pilot.
00:15:25 Jamie: We'll attach the DPA and a network diagram.

00:15:38 (short break in discussion, minor audio pop)

00:16:02 Riley: For the load-run config, do you want us to simulate real user sessions (stateful) or stateless calls?
00:16:09 Aisha: Both. Stateful for chat-like flows and stateless for quick lookups. Probably 60% chat-like to 40% stateless.
00:16:17 Riley: Good, we'll parameterize that.

00:16:45 Martin: On timeline, can you confirm exact dates for deliverables?
00:16:51 Jamie: Proposed: Docs exchanged by 2025-03-21. Baseline run week of 2025-03-24. Pilot window 2025-03-31 to 2025-04-25 (4 weeks). Final report by 2025-04-28. Does that work?
00:17:08 Martin: We'll check internal calendars but tentatively yes. Procurement will confirm.

00:17:35 Leo: A security nuance: if you offer BYOK on Dedicated, we need proof of key separation and key rotation policies. Also, HSM-backed keys are preferred.
00:17:47 Riley: We'll include HSM/BYOK options and rotation docs.

00:18:20 Aisha: Can we get a sample of the audit log event for a redaction? I want to see what fields are included.
00:18:26 Riley: We'll include a sample schema in the follow-up (redaction event with prompt hash, redaction fields, redaction reason, actor).

00:18:44 Jamie: I'll summarize next steps now.
00:18:48 Jamie: 1) Jamie sends SOC2/ISO + vendor questionnaire and DPA by 2025-03-21. 2) Riley schedules baseline run and requests sample corpus by 2025-03-24. 3) BlueCrest provides data samples, redaction rules, and SIEM endpoint by 2025-03-21. 4) Schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2025-03-31.
00:19:06 Martin: That looks right.

00:19:12 (audio: someone typing)

00:19:30 (minor crosstalk)

00:19:45 Jamie: Anything else? If not, we'll close and get you those docs.
00:19:50 Martin: No, thanks everyone. Appreciate the clarity.
00:19:55 Jamie: Thanks all. We'll follow up in writing with the action items and the SOW draft.

00:20:03 (call largely wraps up, remaining time used for calendar invites and some side questions about billing)

Action Items (recorded in transcript):
- Jamie to share SOC 2 and ISO docs, DPA, vendor questionnaire.
- Riley to run baseline + load tests once corpus is provided.
- BlueCrest to provide sample corpus and redaction rules and SIEM endpoints.

End of Transcript.
